questions.stem: Why can only transverse waves be polarised?

options.text: Because transverse waves oscillate in multiple planes perpendicular to the direction of travel, so these can be restricted to one plane
Because longitudinal waves have no amplitude
Because longitudinal waves can only travel through solids

questions.explanation: Transverse waves oscillate in many planes perpendicular to the wave direction. A polarising filter restricts oscillations to a single plane. Longitudinal waves oscillate along the direction of travel, so there are no multiple perpendicular planes to restrict.

questions.stem: In a longitudinal wave, what are the regions where particles are closest together called?
questions.explanation: In a longitudinal wave, compressions are the regions where particles are pushed close together (high pressure). Rarefactions are the regions where particles are spread apart (low pressure). Crests and troughs are features of transverse waves.
